# Rules

<!-- Generated by `prepublish-audit rules --format markdown`; do not edit by hand. -->

Every finding carries one of these rule IDs. Severities are defaults: change them with the
`severity` table in the config (the denylist always stays an error). Disable a rule with
`disable = ["rule.id"]`, or allow it in known-good places with an `[[allow]]` entry.
The coverage rules (`scan.*`, `config.*`, `git.shallow-clone`) can only be disabled or allowed
on the command line (`--disable`, `--allow`). Findings from gitleaks appear as
`gitleaks.<gitleaks-rule-id>`.

## Configuration

### `config.denylist-in-tree`

**Private denylist inside the scanned tree** (default severity: error)

The private denylist file sits inside a tree you are about to publish.

**Fix:** Move the denylist outside every repository, for example to ~/.config/prepublish-audit/.

## Private denylist

### `denylist`

**Private denylist match** (default severity: error)

Text that matches an entry in your private denylist. The entry is never printed; reports show its label or number.

**Fix:** Remove or rename it. If it is allowed in this place, add an indented 'allow:' line under the entry.

## Git history

### `git.author-identity`

**Personal email in commit history** (default severity: warning)

A commit, tag or author email that is not a no-reply address. Public history keeps it forever.

**Fix:** Publish from a fresh history committed with a no-reply address (see https://github.com/deegitech/prepublish-audit/blob/v0.1.0/docs/release-checklist.md).

### `git.shallow-clone`

**Shallow clone: history scan incomplete** (default severity: warning)

The repository is a shallow clone, so older commits were not scanned.

**Fix:** Fetch the full history (actions/checkout with fetch-depth: 0) and scan again.

## Leak heuristics

### `leak.ad-identifier`

**Advertising or analytics account ID** (default severity: warning)

An AdMob/AdSense publisher or app ID, a Google Ads conversion ID, a Meta ad account (act_...) or a Google tag ID.

**Fix:** Keep ad and analytics IDs in build configuration that is not published.

### `leak.apple-developer-id`

**Apple developer account ID** (default severity: warning)

An Apple team ID, App Store Connect key ID or issuer ID, or an AuthKey_<KEYID>.p8 file name.

**Fix:** Keep team and key IDs in local build settings or CI secrets.

### `leak.cloud-account-id`

**Cloud account ID** (default severity: warning)

An AWS account ID inside an ARN.

**Fix:** Use a placeholder account such as 123456789012 in examples.

### `leak.cloud-resource`

**Cloud resource name** (default severity: warning)

A storage bucket (S3, GCS, R2, Azure Blob) or an AWS resource ID such as an EC2 instance.

**Fix:** Read resource names from configuration; use placeholders in docs.

### `leak.confidential-marker`

**Confidentiality marking** (default severity: warning)

Text carrying a confidentiality marking: a confidential or internal-use stamp, a do-not-distribute line or an NDA notice. Marked material should not be published.

**Fix:** Remove the material or get it cleared for publication.

### `leak.email`

**Email address** (default severity: warning)

An email address outside the allowed domains. Addresses of staff and customers are personal data and attract spam and phishing.

**Fix:** Remove it, use a role address on an allowed domain, or add the domain to allowed-email-domains.

### `leak.embedded-git-dir`

**Embedded .git directory** (default severity: warning)

A .git directory inside the published tree or archive ships the complete history of that repository.

**Fix:** Remove the .git directory from the bundle.

### `leak.home-path`

**Absolute home-directory path** (default severity: warning)

An absolute path inside a user's home directory (/Users/<name>, /home/<name>, C:\Users\<name>). It reveals a username and the layout of a developer's machine.

**Fix:** Use relative paths, ~, or an environment variable.

### `leak.identifier-assignment`

**Hard-coded account identifier** (default severity: warning)

A value assigned to a name such as customer_id, account_id, page_id or business_id.

**Fix:** Read the ID from configuration that is not published.

### `leak.internal-host`

**Internal hostname** (default severity: warning)

A hostname on an internal-only suffix (.internal, .corp, .lan, .local, .home.arpa...) or a UNC path.

**Fix:** Use a placeholder host such as db.example.internal, or read the host from configuration.

### `leak.internal-link`

**Link to a private workspace or console** (default severity: warning)

A link into a private workspace or admin console (Google Docs/Drive, Slack, Notion, Jira, Figma, cloud, ads and store consoles...). Such links often carry account IDs and internal names.

**Fix:** Remove the link or replace it with public documentation.

### `leak.internal-name`

**Internal name pattern** (default severity: warning)

A name that matches one of the internal-name patterns in your config (internal-patterns).

**Fix:** Rename it or remove it before publishing.

### `leak.ip-address`

**IP address** (default severity: warning)

A private, shared (VPN/tailnet) or public IP address of a host. Documentation ranges, loopback and well-known public resolvers are ignored.

**Fix:** Replace it with a hostname from configuration or a documentation address (192.0.2.0/24).

### `leak.mounted-volume`

**Mounted volume path** (default severity: warning)

A macOS /Volumes/<name> path: it names a disk on a developer's machine.

**Fix:** Use relative paths or a configurable location.

### `leak.numeric-id`

**Long numeric identifier** (default severity: warning)

A standalone number of 10+ digits: account, customer, campaign, page or user IDs usually look like this.

**Fix:** Move IDs to configuration that is not published, or allow placeholders in config.

### `leak.os-metadata-file`

**Operating-system or IDE metadata file** (default severity: warning)

A .DS_Store, resource fork, thumbnail cache or per-user IDE file. They leak file names, usernames and local paths.

**Fix:** Delete it and add the pattern to .gitignore (or your packaging excludes).

### `leak.payment-card`

**Payment card number** (default severity: error)

A Luhn-valid number with a card-network prefix. Public test cards are ignored.

**Fix:** Remove it; if it is real, treat it as a card data incident.

### `leak.phone-number`

**Phone number** (default severity: warning)

An international phone number (+country code). Staff and customer numbers are personal data.

**Fix:** Remove it or use a fictional number.

## Metadata

### `metadata.author`

**Author or owner metadata** (default severity: warning)

Document, image or media metadata that names a person, organisation or computer (author, artist, last modified by, company, camera owner, host computer...).

**Fix:** Strip metadata (exiftool -all=, or 'Inspect Document' in Office) or set a neutral author.

### `metadata.location`

**Location metadata** (default severity: error)

GPS coordinates or a location tag in an image or video. It can reveal a home or office address.

**Fix:** Strip location data (exiftool -gps:all= -xmp:geotag= -keys:location=) before publishing.

### `metadata.serial`

**Device serial number** (default severity: warning)

A camera or lens serial number in image metadata.

**Fix:** Strip maker and serial metadata before publishing.

## Scan coverage

### `scan.incomplete`

**File could not be fully scanned** (default severity: warning)

The scanner could not inspect this content (too large, unreadable, encrypted or an unsupported container).

**Fix:** Check it by hand, raise the limit, or exclude it explicitly if it is safe.

## Secrets

### `secret.anthropic-api-key`

**Anthropic API key** (default severity: error)

An Anthropic API or admin key (sk-ant-...).

**Fix:** Revoke the key in the Anthropic Console.

### `secret.authorization-header`

**Authorization header credential** (default severity: error)

A literal HTTP Authorization header with Basic credentials or a bearer token.

**Fix:** Rotate the credential; keep headers out of logs, fixtures and docs.

### `secret.aws-access-key-id`

**AWS access key ID** (default severity: error)

An AWS access key ID (AKIA/ASIA...). Usually published together with its secret key.

**Fix:** Deactivate the key in IAM, check CloudTrail for use, and switch to short-lived credentials.

### `secret.aws-secret-access-key`

**AWS secret access key** (default severity: error)

A 40-character AWS secret access key assigned to an aws_secret_access_key-style name.

**Fix:** Deactivate the key pair in IAM and rotate it.

### `secret.credentials-in-url`

**Password in a URL** (default severity: error)

A URL with an embedded user:password@host credential.

**Fix:** Change the password and pass credentials through environment variables or a secret store.

### `secret.generic-assignment`

**Hard-coded credential** (default severity: warning)

A quoted value assigned to a name such as password, secret, token or api_key.

**Fix:** Move the value to an environment variable or secret store; if it is a fake, allow it in config.

### `secret.github-token`

**GitHub token** (default severity: error)

A GitHub personal access, OAuth, app or refresh token.

**Fix:** Revoke it at github.com/settings/tokens (or the app settings) and create a new one.

### `secret.gitlab-token`

**GitLab token** (default severity: error)

A GitLab personal, project, deploy, runner or trigger token.

**Fix:** Revoke the token in GitLab and create a new one.

### `secret.google-api-key`

**Google API key** (default severity: error)

A Google API key (AIza...). Browser keys for Maps or Firebase are meant to ship, but only with application restrictions; unrestricted keys are abused for billing.

**Fix:** Restrict or rotate the key in Google Cloud console; allow it here only if it is a restricted browser key.

### `secret.google-oauth-client-secret`

**Google OAuth client secret** (default severity: error)

A Google OAuth client secret (GOCSPX-...).

**Fix:** Reset the client secret in Google Cloud console.

### `secret.google-oauth-token`

**Google OAuth token** (default severity: error)

A Google OAuth access token (ya29.) or refresh token (1//0...).

**Fix:** Revoke the grant at myaccount.google.com/permissions or in the OAuth client, then rotate.

### `secret.high-entropy-string`

**High-entropy string** (default severity: warning)

A long random-looking token (mixed case and digits, entropy above the threshold) that may be a credential.

**Fix:** Check what it is. Rotate it if it is a credential; otherwise allow it in config.

### `secret.jwt`

**JSON Web Token** (default severity: error)

A signed JSON Web Token. Many are session or service credentials, some long-lived.

**Fix:** Find out what issued it; revoke the session or rotate the signing key if it is still valid.

### `secret.meta-access-token`

**Meta access token** (default severity: error)

A Meta (Facebook/Instagram) Graph API access token (EAA...).

**Fix:** Invalidate it (change the app secret or remove the system user token) and issue a new one.

### `secret.meta-app-token`

**Meta app access token** (default severity: error)

A Meta app access token in app-id|app-secret form.

**Fix:** Reset the app secret in the Meta developer dashboard.

### `secret.npm-token`

**npm access token** (default severity: error)

An npm automation, publish or read token (npm_...).

**Fix:** Revoke it with 'npm token revoke' or on npmjs.com.

### `secret.openai-api-key`

**OpenAI API key** (default severity: error)

An OpenAI API key (sk-... with the T3BlbkFJ marker, or a long sk-proj- key).

**Fix:** Revoke the key in the OpenAI dashboard.

### `secret.private-key`

**Private key** (default severity: error)

A PEM, OpenSSH, PGP or PuTTY private key block. Anyone holding it can impersonate the key owner.

**Fix:** Remove the key, revoke or rotate it, and load keys from a secret store at runtime.

### `secret.pypi-token`

**PyPI API token** (default severity: error)

A PyPI upload token (pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc...).

**Fix:** Delete the token in your PyPI account settings.

### `secret.sensitive-file`

**Sensitive file type** (default severity: error)

A file whose name or extension marks it as a key, credential store or secrets file.

**Fix:** Remove the file from the tree and its history; rotate anything it contained.

### `secret.slack-token`

**Slack token** (default severity: error)

A Slack bot, user, app or configuration token.

**Fix:** Revoke it in the Slack app settings and create a new one.

### `secret.slack-webhook`

**Slack webhook URL** (default severity: error)

A Slack incoming-webhook or workflow URL; anyone with it can post to your workspace.

**Fix:** Delete the webhook in Slack and create a new one.

### `secret.stripe-live-key`

**Stripe live secret key** (default severity: error)

A Stripe live secret or restricted key.

**Fix:** Roll the key in the Stripe dashboard.

### `secret.stripe-test-key`

**Stripe test secret key** (default severity: warning)

A Stripe test-mode secret key: no money moves, but it opens your test data and settings.

**Fix:** Roll the test key in the Stripe dashboard.

### `secret.stripe-webhook-secret`

**Stripe webhook signing secret** (default severity: error)

A Stripe webhook signing secret (whsec_...).

**Fix:** Roll the signing secret for the endpoint in the Stripe dashboard.
